quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: A headlight:

options.text: Helps other drivers see you.
Often distracts other drivers.
Attracts unwanted attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times while riding, even during the day. This is the best way to help others see your motorcycle.

questions.question: When alcohol and drugs are used together, their effects:

options.text: Are less dangerous than when either is used alone.
Often balance out.
Can be stronger than when either is used alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it harder to ride safely. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes them even more dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel slower than 25 mph. Examples include farm equipment, construction machines, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a motorcycle rider has an advantage because:

options.text: The motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
The rider can stay in the left part of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.
Motorcycles stop shorter than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider can stay in the left part of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.
questions.explanation: When parked vehicles are on your right, ride in the left part of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people exiting vehicles, or people walking between cars. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Stopping while turning is difficult because:

options.text: The bike is leaning, so less grip is available for stopping.
The rider is focused on the turn, not on braking.
The brakes do not work when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bike is leaning, so less grip is available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle is leaning, some grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip available for stopping.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
Go through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or lights, if you and another driver arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: A person is considered intoxicated with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____.

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are intoxicated. You cannot legally drive a vehicle if you are intoxicated.

questions.question: To make it easier for others to see you, you should:

options.text: Wear bright-colored clothing while riding.
Wear dark-colored clothing while riding.
Wave your arms while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing while riding.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. This helps other drivers see you any time of day or night.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:

options.text: Help in most situations.
Improve steering.
Cause control problems.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause control problems.
questions.explanation: Locking the brakes causes control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and then apply it again. If your rear brake locks on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a divided roadway is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the roadway.
Traffic signal ahead.
Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Will a DOT-compliant helmet limit a motorcyclist's view of the road?

options.text: Yes, it greatly reduces side vision.
Maybe. Some DOT-compliant helmets limit vision.
No. A DOT-compliant helmet will not limit your side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: No. A DOT-compliant helmet will not limit your side vision.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.

questions.question: Reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn at night.
Help other drivers see you better.
Do not make riding safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing makes you more visible to other drivers. This helps keep you safer.

questions.question: As a rider, you can lessen your chances of an accident by:

options.text: Not looking ahead for dangers.
Not using turn signals so you don't distract other drivers.
Making sure other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To avoid accidents, be visible to other drivers, signal your moves clearly, keep safe distance from other vehicles, watch ahead for problems, and be ready to react to any danger.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Usually causes no problems.
Is a major cause of many motorcycle crashes.
Is not a problem because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking techniques is important for safe riding.

questions.question: Before turning, a motorcyclist should shift gears to:

options.text: Prevent sudden power changes during the turn.
Keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent sudden power changes during the turn.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before you turn. Shifting during a turn can cause sudden power changes that make the rear wheel skid. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When being passed, where should a motorcyclist ride in the lane?

options.text: The right side
The center
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or from ahead. Riding closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation for both of you.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle at night, how can you see bumps in the road?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Watch the rear bumper of the vehicle ahead to see if it bounces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: Use the vehicle ahead to see road conditions at night. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps in the road ahead.

questions.question: As your motorcycle accelerates, you will need to:

options.text: Shift to a higher gear.
Shift to a lower gear.
Put the bike in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a higher gear.
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle accelerates, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Look ahead at the road.
Be ready to avoid hazards.
Turn your headlights off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlights off during the day.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always scan the road ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT protect you from serious injury in a crash?

options.text: A DOT-compliant helmet.
A leather jacket.
A sweatshirt.

questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet protects your head and neck. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects against injury. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the turn.
Slow down while turning.
Use only the handlebars to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Lean your body in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you start the turn, not during it.

questions.question: A wobble, or sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars, is usually caused by:

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
The front wheel not being fastened tightly to the frame.
Hitting something with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
questions.explanation: A wobble is shaking of the front wheel and handlebars from side to side. Most wobbles are caused by incorrect tire pressure, poor weight distribution, or unsuitable accessories.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, ride:

options.text: In the left part of your lane.
In the right part of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane. This keeps you away from opening car doors and people stepping out between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane to have more space around you.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you an escape route.
Encourage other riders to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you an escape route.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you safe from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if you can shift smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if you can shift smoothly.
questions.explanation: Shift gears before starting a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power can make the rear wheel skid.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system links the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: To work properly, a face shield or eye protection must:

options.text: Fasten securely.
Block your side vision so you focus on the road.
Prevent you from wearing eyeglasses or sunglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good face shield or eye protection must have no scratches, resist damage, allow clear side vision, fasten securely, let air through to prevent fogging, and allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: Near the left footrest.
Near the right footrest.
Near the right handle grip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.
